title: Game 3: Magnus vs Hans
notes: Game 3 of 20 in the experiment. Magnus (the learner) reads his notebook before every move; Hans (the control) has no notebook.
result_text: Draw: not enough pieces left to checkmate

new_lessons: In king-and-pawn endgames, calculate the key squares precisely—don't rely on general "opposition" intuition when a pawn is nearby.
Before moving a knight to a square attacked by enemy pawns or pieces, confirm it isn't simply captured for free next move.
When your king endgame is drawn or winning, double-check candidate king moves against the specific key-square rule rather than assuming any safe-looking move works.
